claims.text: Hypothyroidism: levothyroxine, adjusted until TSH is in the midnormal range
claims.quote: Levothyroxine, adjusted until TSH levels are in midnormal range (1)

claims.text: Levothyroxine dose: usual maintenance 75 to 150 mcg orally once a day; otherwise healthy young or middle-aged adults can start at 100 mcg or 1.7 mcg/kg once a day
claims.quote: Levothyroxine is preferred; the usual maintenance dose is 75 to 150 mcg orally once a day, depending on age, body mass index, and absorption (for pediatric treatment, see Hypothyroidism in Infants and Children). In young or middle-aged patients who are otherwise healthy, the starting dose of levothyroxine can be 100 mcg or 1.7 mcg/kg orally once a day.

claims.text: Heart disease: start low, usually 25 mcg once a day, adjusting every 6 weeks until the maintenance dose is reached
claims.quote: In patients with heart disease, therapy is begun with low doses of levothyroxine, usually 25 mcg once a day. The dose is adjusted every 6 weeks until maintenance dose is achieved.

claims.text: Older patients: also start low, usually 25 mcg once a day; maintenance doses may be lower
claims.quote: In older patients, levothyroxine therapy is begun with low doses, usually 25 mcg once a day. Maintenance doses may also need to be lower in older patients.

claims.text: Dose may need raising: in pregnancy, and with drugs that reduce T4 absorption (calcium, iron, magnesium, cholestyramine) or speed its clearance (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, topiramate)
claims.quote: The maintenance dose may need to be increased in patients who are pregnant. Dose may also need to be increased if medications that decrease T4 absorption (eg, calcium, iron, magnesium, cholestyramine) or increase its metabolic clearance (eg, rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, topiramate) are administered concomitantly.

claims.text: Secondary hypothyroidism: TSH can't guide the dose; aim for a midnormal free T4 instead
claims.quote: The dose used should be the lowest that restores serum TSH levels to the midnormal range (though this criterion cannot be used in patients with secondary hypothyroidism). In secondary hypothyroidism the dose of levothyroxine should achieve a free T4 level in the midnormal range.

claims.text: Secondary hypothyroidism: hold levothyroxine until cortisol secretion is shown to be adequate (or cortisol is given), because it could precipitate adrenal crisis
claims.quote: In patients with secondary hypothyroidism, levothyroxine should not be given until there is evidence of adequate cortisol secretion (or cortisol therapy is given), because levothyroxine could precipitate adrenal crisis.

claims.text: Subclinical hypothyroidism with TSH > 10 mIU/L: likely to progress to overt hypothyroidism; treat with levothyroxine even if asymptomatic
claims.quote: In patients with serum TSH > 10 mIU/L (> 10 microIU/mL), there is a high likelihood of progression to overt hypothyroidism with low serum levels of free T4 within the next 10 years. These patients are also more likely to have hypercholesterolemia and atherosclerosis. They should be treated with levothyroxine, even if they are asymptomatic.

claims.text: TSH between 4.5 and 10: a levothyroxine trial is reasonable if symptoms of early hypothyroidism (e.g., fatigue, depression) are present
claims.quote: For patients with TSH levels between 4.5 and 10 mUI/L, (4.5 and 10 microIU/L) a trial of levothyroxine is reasonable if symptoms of early hypothyroidism (eg, fatigue, depression) are present.

claims.text: Myxedema coma: a large initial IV dose of T4 (300 to 500 mcg) or T3 (25 to 50 mcg), plus glucocorticoids because central adrenal insufficiency can't be excluded at first; don't rewarm rapidly (hypotension, arrhythmias)
claims.quote: Patients require a large initial dose of T4 (300 to 500 mcg IV) or T3 (25 to 50 mcg IV). The intravenous maintenance dose of T4 is 75 to 100 mcg once a day and of T3, 10 to 20 mcg twice a day until T4 can be given orally. Glucocorticoids are also given because the possibility of central hypothyroidism and central adrenal insufficiency usually cannot be initially excluded. The patient should not be rewarmed rapidly, which may precipitate hypotension or arrhythmias.

claims.text: Hyperthyroidism, by cause: radioactive iodine, methimazole or propylthiouracil, beta blockers, iodine, or thyroidectomy
claims.quote: Treatment of hyperthyroidism depends on the cause (1) but may include the following: Radioactive iodine Methimazole or propylthiouracil Beta-blockers Iodine Thyroidectomy

claims.text: Radioactive iodine (iodine-131): the most common U.S. treatment; often the treatment of choice for Graves disease and toxic nodular goiter
claims.quote: In the United States, iodine-131 is the most common treatment for hyperthyroidism. Radioiodine is often recommended as the treatment of choice for Graves disease and toxic nodular goiter in all patients, including children.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Radioactive sodium iodine

claims.text: After radioiodine: 25 to 50% are hypothyroid 1 year later, and most eventually need thyroid hormone replacement
claims.quote: When sufficient iodine-131 is given to cause euthyroidism, approximately 25 to 50% of patients become hypothyroid 1 year later, and the incidence continues to increase yearly. Thus, most patients eventually become hypothyroid and require thyroid hormone replacement.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Radioactive sodium iodine

claims.text: No radioiodine in pregnancy or lactation: it enters breast milk and crosses the placenta, causing hypothyroidism in the infant or fetus
claims.quote: Radioactive iodine is not used during lactation because it can enter breast milk and cause hypothyroidism in the infant. It is not used during pregnancy because it crosses the placenta and can cause severe fetal hypothyroidism.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Radioactive sodium iodine

claims.text: Methimazole (preferred): start 5 to 20 mg orally 1 to 3 times a day; TSH lags T4 and T3 by weeks, so once T4 and T3 normalize lower to 2.5 to 10 mg once a day; control usually takes 2 to 3 months
claims.quote: Methimazole is the preferred medication. The usual starting dose of methimazole is 5 to 20 mg orally 1 to 3 times a day. Normalization of TSH lags normalization of T4 and T3 levels by weeks. Therefore, when T4 and T3 levels normalize, the dosage is decreased to the lowest effective amount, usually methimazole 2.5 to 10 mg once a day in order to avoid inducing hypothyroidism. Control generally is achieved in 2 to 3 months.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Methimazole and propylthiouracil

claims.text: Propylthiouracil (PTU): only in special situations (e.g., first trimester of pregnancy, thyroid storm), because of severe liver failure in some patients
claims.quote: Because of severe liver failure in some patients < 40 years old, especially children, propylthiouracil is recommended only in special situations (eg, during the first trimester of pregnancy, in thyroid storm).
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Methimazole and propylthiouracil

claims.text: Antithyroid drug adverse effects: rash, allergic reactions, abnormal liver function (hepatic failure with PTU), and reversible agranulocytosis in about 0.1%; after agranulocytosis, don't switch to the other drug, use radioiodine or surgery
claims.quote: Adverse effects include rash, allergic reactions, abnormal liver function (including hepatic failure with propylthiouracil), and, in approximately 0.1% of patients, reversible agranulocytosis. Patients allergic to one medication can be switched to the other, but cross-sensitivity may occur. If agranulocytosis occurs, the patient cannot be switched to the other medication; other therapy (eg, radioiodine, surgery) should be used.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Methimazole and propylthiouracil

claims.text: Beta blockers (propranolol; atenolol or metoprolol): for adrenergic symptoms such as tachycardia, tremor, anxiety and eyelid lag
claims.quote: Symptoms and signs of hyperthyroidism due to adrenergic stimulation may respond to beta-blockers; propranolol has had the greatest use, but atenolol or metoprolol are alternatives. Manifestations that typically respond to beta-blockers include: Tachycardia Tremor Some mental symptoms (eg, anxiety) Eyelid lag

claims.text: Why beta blockers early: antithyroid drugs usually take several weeks to become fully effective, so beta blockers cover the tachycardia, especially in older patients
claims.quote: Beta-blockers are also indicated for tachycardia with hyperthyroidism, especially in older patients, because antithyroid medications usually take several weeks to become fully effective.

claims.text: Thyroid storm, PTU: preferred, because high doses (over 800 mg a day) also partly block T4-to-T3 conversion
claims.quote: Propylthiouracil is preferred for the treatment of thyroid storm, because the high dosages used (over 800 mg a day) partially block the peripheral conversion of T4 to T3 in addition to decreasing production in the thyroid.
claims.locator: Treatment of Hyperthyroidism, Methimazole and propylthiouracil

claims.text: Thyroid storm, PTU dose: 600 mg orally given before iodine, then 200–400 mg every 6–8 hours
claims.quote: Propylthiouracil: 600 mg orally given before iodine, then 200–400 mg every 6–8 hours

claims.text: Thyroid storm, iodine: e.g., 5 drops (0.25 mL) of saturated potassium iodide solution orally every 6 hours
claims.quote: Iodine: 5 drops (0.25 mL) saturated solution of potassium iodide orally every 6 hours

claims.text: Thyroid storm, propranolol: 60–80 mg orally every 4–6 hours, adjusted for heart rate and blood pressure
claims.quote: Propranolol: 60–80 mg orally every 4–6 hours with appropriate adjustment for heart rate and blood pressure

claims.text: Thyroid storm, glucocorticoids: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV every 8 hours or dexamethasone 2 mg IV every 6 hours
claims.quote: Glucocorticoids: Hydrocortisone 100 mg intravenously every 8 hours or Dexamethasone 2 mg intravenously every 6 hours

claims.text: Thyroid storm, supportive care: IV dextrose, correct dehydration and electrolytes, cooling blanket for hyperthermia, antiarrhythmics if needed for AF, and treat the underlying disorder (e.g., infection)
claims.quote: Intravenous dextrose solutions | Correction of dehydration and electrolyte imbalance | Cooling blanket for hyperthermia | Antiarrhythmics (eg, calcium channel blockers, adenosine, beta-blockers) if necessary for atrial fibrillation | Treatment of underlying disorder, such as infection

claims.text: After the storm: definitive therapy, thyroid ablation with iodine-131 or surgery
claims.quote: Definitive therapy after control of the crisis via ablation of the thyroid with iodine-131 or surgical treatment
